## Recipe semantics (git/gh/bash) — the core question

- **`\|\|` chaining is correct.** Line 1 (`probe \|\| fetch \|\| true`): fetch fires only on probe miss; `\|\| true` bounds a failed fetch without aborting. Line 2: `SUBJECT=$(cmd)` carries cmd's exit status, so a local `git log` failure (rc 128 on missing/`null` object, stderr suppressed deliberately) fires the fallback exactly and only on local-read failure; a successful local read never triggers a spurious remote call.
- **No FALSE-PASS path.** Certification is the string-contains check on `$SUBJECT`. Staleness can only manifest as object ABSENCE (content-addressing: a locally-present `$MERGE_SHA` object is byte-identical to the remote commit), so a resolved subject is always the true merge commit's subject — a foreign SHA fails the contains-check as designed.
- **No SILENT-POST path.** The `gh api ... \| head -1` pipeline masks gh's non-zero exit (pipeline status = `head`'s 0), so a 404/`null` yields `SUBJECT=""` with "success" status — but the prose explicitly closes this: "an EMPTY `$SUBJECT` after both reads is an ABORT (cannot certify), never a silent post," and an empty subject also fails the contains-check. Both routes end in ABORT.
- **`.commit.message \| head -1` ≡ `%s`** (first line of full message = subject). `{owner}/{repo}` placeholder resolution from the ambient repo is standard `gh api` behavior, consistent with the sibling `gh pr view <PR> --json mergeCommit` in the same section (also ambient-resolved); a resolution failure degrades to empty `$SUBJECT` → ABORT.
- **Register/indentation:** 6-space code block under the 2-space Success-bullet paragraphs renders correctly (2 content-indent + 4); heading/incident-citation style matches the sibling "Authoritative merge-SHA derivation (#1722)" paragraph.
